What's the difference between a debit card and a credit card?
A debit card spends money you have. A credit card spends money you borrowed.
Only the borrowed one builds your credit score.

What's the difference between a stop loss and a stop limit?
A stop loss guarantees the exit, not the price. A stop limit guarantees the price, not the exit.
Neither does both.

What's the difference between a million and a billion?
A million seconds is 12 days. A billion seconds is 32 years.
One word. A thousand times the size.

What's the difference between a correction and a bear market?
A correction: at least 10% off the high, usually over in months. A bear market: at least 20%, and recovery often took years.
Scary words, exact numbers.
Share this with your best mate who calls every 10% dip a crash, before he panic-sells the next one.

What's the difference between saving and investing?
Saving keeps your number still. Investing lets it move, both ways.
At 2% inflation, 100 buys half a video game in 35 years.
Share this with your best mate who's still "saving up", so he doesn't find out the expensive way.

What's the difference between a market order and a limit order?
A market order guarantees the trade, not the price. A limit order guarantees the price, not the trade.
In a fast market, that gap is real money.

What's the difference between margin and leverage?
Leverage is a ratio. Margin is real money, locked up.
At 1:100, a 10,000 position locks up 100 of your cash.
Share this with your best mate who thinks high leverage means high risk, before he sizes a trade on the wrong number.

What's the difference between going long and going short?
Long: buy at 100, sell at 130, you made 30. Short: borrow and sell at 100, buy back at 70, you made 30.
But a stock can only fall to zero. It can rise forever.
Share this with your best mate who wants to short his first stock, before he finds out where the risk ends.

What's the difference between win rate and expectancy?
Win rate counts how often. Expectancy counts how much.
70% winners can still lose money. 38% winners can still make it.
Share this with your best mate who brags about his win rate, before he wonders where the money went.
